name: Unify physical access revocation with the offboarding trigger and evidence roster review
description: Drive badge revocation from the same event that removes logical access, distinguish sensitive areas from general facility access, and make the roster review produce evidenced revocations rather than an acknowledgement.
responsible_role: Facilities or Workplace Operations, with Security accountable for the review

steps.action: Add physical access revocation to the offboarding checklist driven by the HR termination event, alongside logical deprovisioning.
Separate the badge access model into general facility access and access to server rooms and media storage.
Set a committed revocation timeframe in the physical security policy, chosen from measured performance.
Establish a roster review cadence with a named reviewer for each area.
Require the review to record a per-holder decision and to evidence the revocation of access identified for removal.
Reconcile the roster against current personnel records each cycle and retain the reconciliation as part of the review record.
Bring contractors, visitors, and maintenance personnel into the model, with escort requirements where they apply.

implementation_considerations: Badge systems are frequently administered by a landlord or building operator rather than by the entity, which changes revocation from a configuration change into a service request with its own turnaround. Measure that turnaround before committing to a timeframe.
Where the entity occupies shared space, distinguish building-level access from access to its own suite; conflating them produces findings that are not the entity's to fix.
For a largely remote workforce the roster is small and the review is cheap; the common failure is that nobody owns it, not that it is burdensome.
typical_duration: Weeks, gated by the badge system administrator's responsiveness rather than by internal work.
prerequisites: Clarity on who administers the badge system

verification_method.how: Sample terminations after the change and confirm badge deactivation occurred within the committed timeframe, and confirm the most recent roster review reconciles to personnel records with evidenced revocations.

residual_risk_note: Physical keys, tailgating, and access granted informally by colleagues sit outside a badge-based control and are addressed by awareness and layout rather than by roster hygiene.
period_limitation_note: Revoking retained access now does not change the fact that it was retained during an elapsed period. Where an exception has been identified, this reduces recurrence.
notes: Where facilities are hosted, this remediation applies only to the entity's own offices; the data centre dependency is addressed by REM-PHYSEC-002.
